title: Bird Feeder: integrating generated audio into a quiet desktop bird garden
author: birdfeedergame
selftext:
Bird Feeder is a pixel-art desktop bird garden in development. The attached 24-second clip is captured gameplay: scattering food, petting birds, and watching them drink. Posting from the game's development account.



Development uses AI-assisted coding and generated visual/audio assets, including ElevenLabs audio. One practical lesson has been that generating a sound is only part of making it comfortable in a desktop game. Earlier feedback called out abrupt ambience and unwanted background sounds alongside bird calls.



The current audio setup separates ambient layers from action cues. Food scattering, feeder refills, and decoration placement have separate clips triggered by their respective actions, with a separate pour sound for nectar. The generation prompts ask for one short, isolated gesture without voices, birds, music, or a background noise bed, so a refill doesn't also introduce an unrelated soundscape.



There was also an implementation issue: fading the ambience in decibels produced a noticeable dip between layers. The transition now fades linear amplitudes with overlapping players. That still needs listening in context; a clip sounding pleasant on its own doesn't establish that repeated triggers and transitions are comfortable over a longer session.



For anyone integrating generated audio into a quiet game, how do you test repetition and transitions over time? Feedback on any abrupt sound or distracting movement in this clip is welcome too.
